composite_title: Canvas's operator-owed queue — five items, one sitting
composite_question: Operation Datum closed on 2026-09-15 and left no successor. What remains is the tail that only you can clear. Each section below states what was measured this session, not what the carried-tail table claimed — three of the eleven Datum findings were stale entries in exactly that kind of table. Two sections are actions (a click, a memo); three are directions for work we would then do. Ruling ‘defer’ on any of them is a real answer and is recorded as one.

sections.title: ① The mermaid trust grant — one click, and it is the cheapest item here
sections.question: Both of Canvas's dual-channel dogfood canvases — what/context/context_canvas_surface_legs.canvas and what/decisions/adr_004_production_code_layout.canvas — render their mermaid channel as raw source to any first-open viewer, behind an un-actioned Obsidian trust prompt. Both machine checks pass green. Grant the trust and re-open them?
sections.rec_label: Do it — one click, and an agent must not make a trust decision for you
sections.analysis:
• Why it matters more than it looks. These two are the pair pattern_diagrammatic_context cites BY NAME as its motivating example. The vault's own showcase of dual-channel authoring is the thing rendering half-broken to a new reader.
  • It is the F-P4-3 family. Found by sight, not by a machine check — the first two runs of visual_capture.py certified the geometry of both canvases and showed the mermaid channel as raw source. Every automated gate was green throughout.
  • ⛔ Why an agent will not click it. A trust prompt is a security decision about executing content. Clicking it on your behalf is exactly the class of action that requires a human, and no amount of “it is obviously fine” changes that.
  • Verify after clicking: re-open both canvases and confirm the diagram renders as a diagram. Then both are fully certified rather than “geometry certified, diagram channel unverified.”

recommendation.rationale: Grant it. It is one click, it costs nothing, it is reversible, and it converts the vault's two flagship dual-channel artifacts from partially-certified to fully-certified.
key_factors: Unblocks full certification of both dogfood canvases
The pair the ruled pattern cites by name
risks: None material — it is a local Obsidian trust setting on your own vault
next_actions: Click Allow, re-open both canvases, confirm the diagram renders

sections.title: ② Memo #20 to Rosetta — one delivery, two payloads
sections.question: Rosetta accepted ADR-011's migration recipe in good faith and fired it into .adna/ at template release v8.11 on 2026-09-11. A-8 shipped the same day and made that recipe incomplete. Send memo #20 carrying (a) the ADR-011 erratum and (b) the derivability proposal?
sections.rec_label: Send — the erratum is owed, and it gives the proposal a concrete ask
sections.analysis:
• What they need to know. Completing the field-shape half from our table clears A-2 ×2 and A-6, then trips A-8, because the table never said to add production. The fix is one new row.
  • ⚠ This is not their error. They verified at the object before accepting, returned two facts we did not have, and scoped the release to “8 files… NOT the fleet.” The stale recipe is ours.
  • Why one memo, not two. The erratum is concrete and actionable; the derivability proposal is doctrine. Alone, the proposal is only an offer — together, the memo has a real ask. And re-probing their lease once is cheaper than twice.
  • ⛔ ack_required: true. Our outbound default is false, and Rosetta measured that their reply-owed sweep filters on that flag — so four Canvas memos reported as “nothing owed” while memo #13 sat asking for a ruling. This one asks a question; it must say so in a way a machine sweep can see.
  • Next free number is #20, re-derived across two independent populations (frontmatter and prose) — both agree at 19.

recommendation.rationale: Send it, as one memo with both payloads and ack_required: true. Re-probe their lease at act time and hold if they hold one — a staged memo is not a refused one.
key_factors: The erratum is owed to a peer who acted on our recipe
Gives the doctrine proposal a concrete ask
One lease re-probe instead of two
risks: If their lease is live at act time it stages rather than sends — that is the correct behaviour, not a failure
next_actions: Re-probe Rosetta's lease at act time
Deliver untracked into their tree; never commit there

sections.title: ③ The certification corpus exercises 12 of 40 schema enum values
sections.question: Datum P4b shipped a schema-conformance test that publishes its own coverage: the 12 fixtures exercise 12 of 40 declared enum values, and two enums — edge.styleAttributes.arrow (0/7) and edge.fromEnd (0/2) — are exercised not at all. Widen the corpus, and how far?
sections.rec_label: Partial — cover the two zero-coverage enums only
sections.analysis:
• What is already guarded. P3's declared-state check catches an enum vanishing, and P4b pins the declared totals, so deleting an enum now fails. Coverage is about catching a narrowing — a legal value quietly dropped.
  • Why the two zero-coverage enums are different. Everything else has at least one value exercised, so a fixture touches it. arrow and fromEnd are touched by nothing — they are the only ones where a partial narrowing is completely invisible.
  • ⛔ Why not bulk-add all 28. The fixtures sit behind the certification gate (12/12) and carry downstream meaning as the Standard's reference corpus. Rewriting them wholesale to satisfy a coverage number is the “editing a disagreement into agreement” move this vault has a standing rule against.
  • ⚠ Honest limit either way. Coverage is a property of the corpus, not of the suite. Whatever we do, the number stays published on the face of the result so it is never read as complete.

recommendation.rationale: Partial. Add fixture coverage for arrow and fromEnd only — the two places where a narrowing is currently invisible — and leave the other 28 values as published, named, accepted exposure.
key_factors: The zero-coverage pair is the only genuinely blind spot
Deletion is already caught by the declared-totals pin
Touching the reference corpus has downstream consequences
risks: Even after this, 26 of 40 values remain unexercised — the published figure moves but does not disappear
next_actions: Extend one fixture (or add one) to exercise arrow and fromEnd
Re-derive the coverage figure; do not hand-edit the ratchet

sections.title: ④ skill_l1_upgrade.md — the RFC1918 literals ADR-012 left open
sections.question: ADR-012's own correction found a fourth file its §Decision 3 never saw: how/skills/skill_l1_upgrade.md carries RFC1918 literals (3 × 10.42.0.x, re-verified present 2026-09-16) in a GitHub-public repo. It is template-inherited. Remediate locally, push upstream, or leave?
sections.rec_label: Upstream — remediating our copy fixes one vault of many
sections.analysis:
• Why not just redact ours. The file arrived at Canvas genesis from the template (created 2026-03-21). The same literals sit in every vault forked from it. Fixing our copy makes Canvas clean and the fleet no safer, and it removes the very signal that would prompt the durable fix.
  • Calibration, unchanged from ADR-012. These are RFC1918 addresses on a private overlay — not internet-routable, and knowing them grants no access. Reconnaissance material in a class its owner rules unpublishable; not a credential leak. gitleaks passes and is correct to.
  • Same shape as ADR-011's 196-file legacy — a template-inherited defect whose fix belongs in the template channel, which is Rosetta's.
  • Option: fold into memo #20. That memo is already going to Rosetta with two payloads; a third is cheap. The counter-argument is that it dilutes an erratum that deserves a clear reply.

recommendation.rationale: Route it upstream rather than remediating unilaterally — but raise it as its own item, not as a third payload on memo #20, so the ADR-011 erratum keeps a clean ask.
key_factors: Template-inherited: our copy is one of many
Not a credential leak — calibration already agreed with two peers
The durable fix is in a channel we do not own
risks: Upstream is slower than a local redaction
Our copy stays public in the meantime — accepted by ADR-012's fix-forward ruling
next_actions: Raise with Rosetta as a template-channel item
Record the disposition in ADR-012 so the open item closes

sections.title: ⑤ F-DT-8 — the session file is a registry too
sections.question: Datum found its own session file sitting status: active, phase: "Act 0 → P0", work log unappended, two days and four commits later — spanning two operator rulings. It is hand-maintained, read by the cold-start ritual and by any peer looking for a lease, and nothing fails when it goes stale. Build a freshness check, send it upstream, or leave it filed?
sections.rec_label: Leave filed — it is real, and it is not Canvas's surface
sections.analysis:
• It is a genuine instance of the campaign's own target — the forbidden third state (correct-ish today, hand-maintained, read by nothing that fails), found in the campaign's own session file on the day it reached the phase about it.
  • ⛔ Why Datum did not fix it. The charter's definition of done is scoped to canvas_std vocabulary registries. Widening at P3 on a fresh finding is precisely the scope creep P2's ruling was careful to avoid — and a campaign that quietly grows to cover whatever it trips over stops having a definition of done at all.
  • Why not a local gate #11. Session protocol is standard-side, not Canvas-side. A Canvas-only freshness gate would make this vault compliant and teach the fleet nothing — the same argument that sent the derivability proposal upstream instead of into how/gates/.
  • The cheap half already happened: this session's file was written as the work ran rather than at the end, and the closed one carries a reconstruction labelled as a reconstruction.

recommendation.rationale: Leave filed. It belongs with the derivability proposal as a standard-side concern; building a Canvas-local check would be cheap compliance that teaches the fleet nothing.
key_factors: Datum deliberately declined it on scope grounds
The behavioural half is already being practised
risks: Left filed, it depends on habit — and Datum's own finding is that habit does not transfer by having written the finding down
next_actions: Keep it in the derivability proposal's orbit
Revisit if a second stale-lease incident occurs
